# KBD Constraints — flint-realtime-fabric

> The canonical constraint set the per-change QA gate validates against. Read by
> `/kbd-execute`'s QA step (and the `qa-gate.sh` helper) after a change reaches DONE,
> before archive. Source of truth: `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/PROMETHEUS-BASE-RULES.md`, and
> `~/.claude/rules/rust/*`. Severity drives the gate: **BLOCKING** fails the change
> (→ mark BLOCKED + refine); HIGH/MEDIUM are reported but do not block.

## Legend

- **BLOCKING** — a violation fails the QA gate; the change is marked BLOCKED in
  `progress.json` and must be refined before archive.
- **HIGH / MEDIUM** — reported in the refinement log; reviewed, not auto-blocking.

---

## Architecture (BLOCKING)

- **A1 — Dependency direction.** Nothing in `frf-domain` or `frf-app`/`frf-ports` may
  import an adapter crate (`frf-broker-*`, `frf-authz-*`, `frf-store-*`, `frf-media-*`,
  `frf-bridge-*`, `frf-identity-*`, `frf-policy-*`, `frf-crdt`, `frf-postgres-cdc`).
  Composition happens only in `frf-gateway`.
  *Check:* the `[dependencies]` of `frf-domain` and `frf-app` contain no adapter crate.
- **A2 — One port per adapter.** Each `frf-*` adapter implements exactly one port trait
  and does not reach into another adapter crate.
- **A3 — Proto is frozen.** No edit to `proto/flint/v1/*.proto` (frozen at `proto-v1`).
  A wire-breaking change is a NEW proto version. Non-Rust SDKs generate from the source
  proto — no forked copy committed under `sdks/`.

## Rust quality gates (BLOCKING)

- **R1 — Compiles.** `cargo check --workspace` is clean.
- **R2 — Clippy.** `cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic`
  is clean, plus the `--features frf-gateway/dev-endpoints` and `--tests` passes.
- **R3 — No library `unwrap()`/`expect()`.** `clippy::unwrap_used` / `expect_used` are
  denied at the workspace level; they are allowed only in tests (`clippy.toml`). `anyhow`
  only at binary edges (`frf-gateway`, `frf-cli`).
- **R4 — Formatted.** `cargo fmt --check --all` is clean.
- **R5 — File size.** No hand-authored file over **500 lines** (any language or
  format). Split into a directory module when approaching it. Machine-generated
  dependency lockfiles are exempt because their package managers require the
  native single-file format; do not split or hand-edit them for line count.

## Rust idioms (HIGH)

- **I1 — `#[non_exhaustive]`** on public enums.
- **I2 — Newtype IDs** (`#[repr(transparent)]`) over bare `String` for entity IDs.
- **I3 — `tracing` spans** across every port-boundary call.
- **I4 — MSRV pinned** in the workspace manifest; semver discipline on `frf-domain` and
  SDK crates.

## Security (BLOCKING)

- **S1 — No hardcoded secrets** (API keys, tokens, signing secrets) in any committed
  file. Secrets come from env / a secret manager; validated present at startup.
- **S2 — No auth bypass in a release artifact.** `DEV_NO_AUTH` / `dev-endpoints` are
  compiled out of the production image; never enabled in `compose.yml`.
- **S3 — No sensitive logging.** Never log JWT payloads, relation tuples, or tenant
  identifiers as credentials. (`tenant_id` as a structured observability field is OK.)
- **S4 — Tenant isolation** is enforced at Keto plus the app-layer tenant-equality guard;
  never trust unverified claims downstream.

## Tests & docs (HIGH)

- **T1 — Tests for new behavior.** New logic carries unit/integration tests (AAA); target
  80%+ where practical. Live-service tests gate on env vars and skip cleanly when unset.
- **T2 — Honest surface.** No "healthy but does nothing": a plane/endpoint is either
  functional or explicitly labeled unimplemented/deferred. No doc drift — docs match code.

## Frontend / TypeScript (BLOCKING where the change touches `admin-ui/` or `sdks/ts`)

- **F1 — No `any` types.** TSX over JSX. Components render; hooks coordinate; stores own
  state; services call APIs — no component fetches data directly.

## Spec-backend hygiene (BLOCKING for OpenSpec changes)

- **P1 — Valid spec delta.** Each change carries a `specs/<capability>/spec.md` delta
  (`## ADDED/MODIFIED/...` + a MUST/SHALL body line + `#### Scenario:` blocks) so
  `openspec validate <id>` passes before archive.

---

## Per-change applicability

Not every constraint applies to every change. The gate evaluates the subset relevant to
the files a change touched:

| Change kind | BLOCKING subset |
|-------------|-----------------|
| Rust code | A1–A3, R1–R5, S1–S4, P1 |
| Config / compose | S1, S2, P1 |
| Docs-only | T2 (no drift), P1 |
| Frontend / TS | F1, R5 (size), P1 |
| Tooling / KBD | P1 |

# pri-c014 acceptance B — browser allocation explanation

Result: **Passed**  
Observed: 2026-09-17T13:47:55.203358+00:00  
Dataset: 16,203 synthetic rows  
Campaign: `browser-campaign.json`  
Campaign SHA-256: `8a7b4a9fcd304b025ca8e4e6d8601cf8b5a550d51b67146c86f86538b05caf39`

## Outcome

The current ASO materializer completed the authenticated PostgreSQL → Kratos →
Gate → Fabric → Electric → browser PGlite → PEM campaign in Google Chrome
152.0.7977.84. The isolated target renderer grew by 536,543,232
bytes against the 536,870,912-byte limit. Chromium JavaScript heap grew by
119,808,249 bytes against the 268,435,456-byte limit.
The remaining headroom is 327,680 RSS bytes and
148,627,207 heap bytes.

SQL and PEM graph counts matched for all seven tables, all shape checkpoints
were present at generation 4, all 13 rollback/restart/delete/owner/authority/final-state
checks passed, and all fixture/service/identity cleanup checks passed.

## Measurement method

Chrome ran as an isolated process tree with a unique user-data directory. The
coordinator sampled macOS `ps` RSS for the Chrome root and recursive children,
then selected the renderer with the greatest campaign-time growth. JavaScript
heap came from Chromium `performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize` with
`--enable-precise-memory-info`. The browser loaded the production
`openPGliteReplica`, migration ledger, FRF shape transport, chunk writer,
checkpoint store, committed projector, and replica runtime.

Repeated actual-browser passes on the evolving candidate remained below both
limits. The final source-bound pass is authoritative; earlier passing receipts
are retained to expose run-to-run variation rather than hide it.

The final renderer RSS headroom is only
327,680 bytes. This satisfies the frozen
acceptance threshold but leaves little operational margin and remains a release
risk for later capacity qualification.

## Stage-associated bounds

These values are boundary nets and upper bounds. They do not claim
allocator-specific attribution.

| Boundary | Browser heap | Target-renderer RSS | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Baseline | 7,260,478 | 165,511,168 | Loaded campaign page before PGlite starts. |
| PGlite open | 107,310,318 | — | PGlite/WASM and the versioned base archive dominate browser heap growth. |
| Schema ready | 111,933,987 | — | Replica schema and ledger add 4,623,669 net heap bytes. |
| Empty graph/projector | 108,810,548 | — | Graph runtime and projector add -3,123,439 net heap bytes before rows. |
| Cold fold complete | 125,790,582 | 604,241,920 | Electric folding adds 16,980,034 net heap bytes; renderer growth through this interval is 438,730,752 bytes. |
| Revision published | 112,853,218 | — | Collection occurs during transactional SQL/checkpoint/readback/graph work, so the lower heap boundary is not a negative-allocation claim. |
| Campaign complete | 110,353,032 | 702,054,400 | The 97,812,480-byte RSS increase after the cold-fold stage is an upper bound for SQL/checkpoint/readback/graph publication and retained runtime work. |

`ReplicaWorkerOwner` does not create a second Worker or database. The current
browser implementation runs the materializer in one renderer. The separate
Node durability scenario proves owner disposal, replacement, and authority
fencing; its interval includes database and revision work and therefore remains
an upper bound rather than an owner-only allocation.

## Behavior preserved

The final campaign passed initial SQL/graph parity, complete checkpoints,
gate-summary publication, reference identities, cold rollback, captured-update
rollback, restart without a skipped commit, delete-triggered replacement,
disposed-owner fencing, replacement-owner continuation, and authority-failure
fencing. Final SQL/graph counts and checkpoint generation also matched. The
campaign content-hashed all 26 directly executed/imported source and
configuration inputs before import and after cleanup; both aggregate hashes
were `e381de59e8096e1d27349ec7d6a1d96d162afd73694f61cfeeb1b9d474c903ca`.
No production adoption flag changed.

interpretation.measurementScope: Heap values are stage-associated net boundaries. RSS values are target-renderer net growth and upper bounds; they are not allocator-specific attribution.
interpretation.database: PGlite/WASM plus schema and empty projector reaches the 108810548-byte heap boundary before any Electric fold. Target-renderer RSS reaches 438730752 bytes above baseline by the cold-fold interval.
interpretation.coldFold: The complete cold fold adds 16980034 heap bytes over the empty projector boundary. The 10 ms sampler observed the browser heap peak at the recorded cold-fold stage.
interpretation.sqlCheckpointGraph: V8 collection can lower later heap boundaries, so a lower reading is not treated as a negative allocation. Target-renderer growth from cold-fold stage to completion is a 97812480-byte upper bound for SQL/checkpoint/readback/graph publication and retained runtime work.
interpretation.workerOwner: The current browser path runs in one renderer. ReplicaWorkerOwner is a Web Locks lifecycle owner and does not construct a separate Worker or database; the Node durability scenario proves disposal and replacement fencing but cannot isolate an owner-only allocation.
